title: Estimating Contrast Transfer Function for Cryo-Electron Tomography

steps.title: Verify hardware requirements
steps.instruction: Ensure you are using a Linux computer with at least 32 GB RAM, a CPU with ≥10 cores, and no GPU is required.

steps.title: Install CTFMeasure from source
steps.instruction: Download, extract, compile dependencies, build CTFMeasure, and confirm successful installation.

substeps.instruction: Download the source archive and extract it: `tar -zxvf CTFMeasure_v1.4.0.tar.gz`
Enter the external tools folder: `cd external`
Verify the installation by running the help command: `./bin/CTFMeasure` (the help information should be displayed).

steps.title: Optional: Install pre‑compiled binaries
steps.instruction: Download and extract the binary package, then add the binary folder to your PATH.

substeps.instruction: Add the bin folder to your PATH (bash example): `cd bin` then `export PATH=$PATH:`pwd`` then `cd ..`
If using another shell, replace `export` with the appropriate command, or add the line to `~/.bashrc` for permanent loading.

steps.title: Prepare input data
steps.instruction: Download the example parameter file, unzip it, and place it together with the tilt‑series file.

substeps.instruction: Copy the tilt‑series file `tom1.st` and the parameter file `para_10700.conf` into the same directory.

description: The protocol below describes the estimation of CTF parameters and the absolute tilt angle offset. A dataset “tom1.st” in EMPIAR-107002,3 is used in this protocol and can be downloaded from https://www.ebi.ac.uk/empiar/EMPIAR-10700/. The “.st” file is an MRC file containing all the micrographs of a tilt series, which are arranged in ascending order according to their tilt angles. The “.st” file is usually required by IMOD,4 and can be generated by the IMOD’s subroutine “newstack” that can combine multiple micrographs into a single MRC stack file. Nevertheless, CTFMeasure does not require such a stack file, and, alternatively, uses a micrograph list to describe the input micrographs of a tilt series. That is, both a combined “.st” file and a series of individual micrograph files are accepted for input. The details of creating the micrograph list file for input will be shown in the section “configure the input files” below. In this section, we describe the steps to estimate the CTF parameters and the absolute tilt angle offset of “tom1.st” in EMPIAR-10700.
